transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
Authorities in Bend, Oregon, are expected to provide more details today about the mass
shooting at an elementary school that left three children and a teacher dead.
Oregon Public Broadcasting's Bryce Dole reports it's the city's second high-profile shooting
since 2022.
The shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School has shattered a sense of safety for many who
live in this city, tucked beside Oregon's Cascade Mountains.
On Thursday night, residents gathered in a local park for a vigil.
Among them was Kevin DeRozer, a father of two daughters who said he knew the family
of a victim, who was five.
It's super tough to just know that, you know, it could have been your kids' school maybe
or their campus, and you never want to say goodbye to your kids in the morning and even
assume that you wouldn't, you know, see them again at the end of this school day.
The shooting comes four years after a man shot and killed two people and himself at
a local Safeway.
In both tragedies, bystanders confronted the shooters.
For NPR News, I'm Bryce Dole.
New York Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez has transferred a large sum of money to a
political account supporting Michigan's Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed.
I want to announce that I will be transferring from our campaign in New York one million
dollars to the state of Michigan to help support you all.
It's an unusually large contribution from a House member to a Senate race.
Ocasio-Cortez campaigned with El-Sayed yesterday and has three events planned today in Michigan.
And Trump says he's urged press secretary Katie Zachariah to reconsider staying in a
job, raising doubts about her future as his top spokesperson.
He told reporters at the White House that they spoke this morning and will talk again
when he returns from Georgia.
Earlier today, Trump said he'd leave the decision to her.
The Treasury Department has closed the books on the just-ended fiscal year.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports the federal government ran a deficit of almost $2 trillion.
The government spent a lot more money than it took in last year, $1.992 trillion more
to be exact.
That's the biggest annual deficit since the post-pandemic year of 2021.
Tax revenues were up 3 percent during the year, but spending grew twice as fast.
Just paying interest on the federal debt last year cost the government more than $1.3 trillion.
President Trump's double-digit tariffs did raise some money for the government, but the
Treasury had to refund almost half what those import taxes brought in after the Supreme
Court ruled many of the tariffs are illegal.
It's unusual for the government's finances to be this deep in the red when the country's
not in a recession or fighting a widespread war.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
This is NPR News.
Hurricane Trudy has strengthened into a Category 3 off the Pacific Coast of Mexico.
Forecasters say the storm has maximum sustained winds of 120 miles an hour.
Hurricane warnings have been issued for parts of southwestern Mexico.
Heavy rain could trigger life-threatening flooding and landslides through the weekend.
Demonstrators in France are hoping for a possible alliance tomorrow between student protesters
and the Yellow Vest movement that mobilized against high gas prices and the French government
eight years ago.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports a current economic crisis in the country could bring
the two movements together and what's being billed as a day of anger.
The French Interior Minister says 90 protest marches and 500 separate actions are planned
across the country.
Social media posts indicate that there could be an alliance between the students who are
protesting dilapidated facilities, overcrowded classrooms and a lack of teachers, and a reconstituted
Yellow Vest movement of angry white working-class voters.
Everyone is demanding more government spending and protections against rising energy prices.
But with France mired in debt and with record high borrowing costs, the government has little
room to maneuver.
Meanwhile, stores in some cities are boarding up their windows ahead of tomorrow's protests.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Paris.
The Milwaukee Brewers are headed to the World Series for the first time since 1982.
They beat the Los Angeles Dodgers six to four last night, completing a sweep of the National
League Championship Series.
This is NPR News.

topics.text: Authorities in Bend, Oregon, to release details on elementary school shooting that killed three children and a teacher
Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez transfers $1 million to support Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed
Trump says he urged press secretary Katie Zachariah to reconsider leaving her job
Treasury closes fiscal year with nearly $2 trillion federal deficit, biggest since 2021
Hurricane Trudy strengthens to Category 3 off Pacific Coast of Mexico, warnings issued
French students and Yellow Vest movement may join forces in nationwide protests over economic crisis
Milwaukee Brewers beat Los Angeles Dodgers 6-4 to sweep NLCS, reaching first World Series since 1982
